Wait, `CC(C)(...)` means a carbon with two methyls and another group. So it's a tert-butyl group? Wait, `CC(C)(Y)` usually means a carbon bonded to a methyl, another methyl (via the branch), and Y. So it's a tert-butyl group if Y is the rest. Here Y is `C(=O)NCC1CC1`. So it's a 2-(cyclopropylamino)-2-methylpropanoyl group attached to the phenyl ring!

Acylation typically involves forming an amide bond.
The amide bond here is between the carboxylic acid (or derivative) of 2-(4-(vinylsulfonyl)phenyl)-2-methylpropanoic acid and cyclopropylamine.
